rationale: Raw headers -> short team names (e.g. 'WBC(10^9/L)' -> 'WBC'). Label 'leukemia'/'healthy' -> y = 1/0.

Q-Flag(Blasts/Abn Lympho?), Q-Flag(Blasts?), Q-Flag(Abn Lympho?) dropped: not in the paper's 72 features, 50-100% missing/constant at every site, and they are the analyser's own blast message (shortcut to the label).

In each file, each column contains exactly one value off the instrument's precision grid (e.g. 104.2533936651584). It is that file's column mean used as a fill-in. Every off-grid value is set back to NaN so imputation can be learned inside training folds.
Files whose median HCT < 1 (sites B and C) store HCT as a fraction (L/L). Multiply by 100 so HCT is in % everywhere.
RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, MCHC, RDW-SD, RDW-CV equal to 0 are impossible in a living patient (failed measurement) -> NaN.
When MPV = 0 the analyser did not compute the platelet-index block; PDW, MPV, P-LCR, PCT are set to NaN for that record.
When NEUT%+LYMPH%+MONO%+EO%+BASO% = 0 no differential was reported; the whole differential block (23 columns) is set to NaN. WBC is kept.
NE-/LY-/MO- scattergram positions and widths equal to 0 are 'not measured' (a channel position cannot be 0) -> NaN.
MCHC > 500 g/L is physically impossible (agglutination/optical artefact); MCHC and MCH (both derived from the corrupted RBC count) -> NaN.
Exact duplicate records (all features + label) within a file: keep the first. Identical features with conflicting labels: drop all copies.
Records where WBC, HGB and PLT are all missing carry no screening information and are removed.
All features float64 (NaN-capable), y int8, site/split/cohort categorical. No rows are removed for being extreme - extreme counts are the disease signal.
